name: aidlc-cto
conclusion_quantitative: aidlc-cto (Escalate) specifies 4 of 5 categories: 3 autonomy limits, 9 approval gates, 10+ validation rules, 4 escalation rules; none for clarification rules. Strongest: validation rules.
conclusion_qualitative: aidlc-cto defines the Chief Technology Officer role in an AI-driven development lifecycle: technical authority over architecture, agent allocation, collision detection and merges. Its rules are a chain of gates: an annotation confirmed by the product role before any code, orchestrator approval before invoking agents, and strict verification before merging. A broken main or an unresolved collision is reported and escalated. It sets no clarification rules.

autonomy_limits.conclusion_quantitative: 3 autonomy limits (3 mandatory, 0 advisory; 0 conditional), mostly prose.
autonomy_limits.conclusion_qualitative: There are 3 rules, all strict, none tied to a situation, mostly running text. The CTO never works on main or another agent's branch, never touches a file outside the annotation's list, and does not silently expand its scope.

statements.quote: No work happens on main. No work happens on another agent's branch.
They do not silently expand their scope.
Never touch a file not listed in the annotation's `files_to_touch`

clarification_rules.conclusion_qualitative: The skill never tells the agent to ask the user for missing or unclear information, or to avoid guessing.

approval_gates.conclusion_quantitative: 9 approval gates (9 mandatory, 0 advisory; 1 conditional), mostly list.
approval_gates.conclusion_qualitative: There are 9 rules, all strict, 1 tied to a situation, evenly split between bullet points and running text. Implementation never starts before the CPO confirms the annotation, and execution agents are never invoked without the orchestrator's approval of the brief; work waits for that confirmation.

statements.quote: Begins implementation before annotation is confirmed by CPO
Invokes execution agents without orchestrator permission
**Rule 1: Annotation before code. Always.**
Work does not begin until confirmation is received.
**Rule 3: Orchestrator permission before execution agent invocation.**
Work does not begin before approval.
Wait for explicit CPO confirmation before proceeding
Request orchestrator approval with the brief
Never begin implementation before CPO confirmation is received

validation.conclusion_quantitative: 10+ validation rules (10 mandatory, 0 advisory; 1 conditional), mostly list.
validation.conclusion_qualitative: There are 10 or more rules (the first 10 are kept), all strict, 1 tied to a situation, mostly bullet points. Nothing is merged with failing tests, analyzer errors or lint violations, no agent starts without a clean collision check, and before merging the CTO verifies the quality and design sign-offs, runs the analyzer, and checks main is green with the full test suite.

statements.quote: Merges with failing tests, analyzer errors, or lint violations
No execution agent starts work without a clean collision check.
No commit with analyzer errors reaches a PR.
Run collision detection (Protocol 2) — must be CLEAR before proceeding
Verify CQO sign-off exists in KB
Verify CDO sign-off exists in KB
Pull the branch, run analyzer — must be 0 errors
Verify main is green after merge — run full test suite
If any field is missing, the annotation is incomplete and must not be delivered to the CPO.
Never merge a PR with any failing test, analyzer error, or missing PR description field

escalation.conclusion_quantitative: 4 escalation rules (4 mandatory, 0 advisory; 2 conditional), mostly list.
escalation.conclusion_qualitative: There are 4 rules, all strict, 2 tied to a situation, evenly split between bullet points and running text. A broken main stops everything: the CTO reports it to the orchestrator and does not start feature work or absorb the fix. Collisions it cannot resolve are escalated to the orchestrator.

statements.quote: Absorbs a broken main into a feature branch — reports and stops
**Rule 7: Broken main stops everything.**
If main is broken at session open, the CTO stops, reports to the orchestrator, and does not begin feature work until main is green.
If conflict cannot be resolved by these methods: escalate to orchestrator
